turns.content: Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—can you tell me how long you’ve been feeling sad, and whether the sadness is constant or comes and goes? Doctor: Also, when do you hear voices (all day vs certain times), and are they telling you to harm yourself or anyone else?

Patient: It’s been about four months of feeling persistently sad, mostly constant rather than coming and going. I hear the voices almost all the time now, and they’re telling me I’m worthless, but they don’t tell me to hurt myself or anyone else.

Doctor: Thank you. Have you had any episodes of mania or hypomania—like needing far less sleep, unusually high energy, pressured speech, or risky/impulsive behavior? Also, any substance use (alcohol, cannabis, stimulants) or recent medication changes before the voices and sadness started?

Patient: I haven’t had any times where I felt unusually high energy or needed very little sleep, and I haven’t done anything risky or impulsive. I don’t use alcohol, cannabis, or stimulants, and there haven’t been any medication changes before this started.

Doctor: I’m going to ask: do the voices sound like they’re coming from inside your head or outside your body, and have you had any thoughts of suicide or self-harm (even if you wouldn’t act on them)? Doctor: Also, have you ever experienced these symptoms before, and do they seem to worsen with stress or around the same time each day?

Patient: The voices feel like they’re coming from inside my head, and I haven’t had any thoughts about suicide or hurting myself. I haven’t had these symptoms before, and they seem to be pretty constant rather than clearly tied to stress or a specific time of day.

Doctor: Thanks—one more: how old are you, and is there any history in you or your family of bipolar disorder, schizophrenia/psychosis, or major depression? Also, have you had any recent medical issues (fever, seizures, head injury) or symptoms that might suggest substance/medical causes (new headaches, confusion, vision changes)?

Patient: I’m 23 years old, and I don’t know of any family history of bipolar disorder, schizophrenia/psychosis, or major depression. I haven’t had any recent fever, seizures, head injury, or unusual headaches, confusion, or vision changes.

Doctor: Given 4 months of persistent depressed mood with near-continuous, inside-the-head voices that say you’re worthless, and no history of mania/hypomania or substance/medication triggers, I’m concerned about a psychotic depression versus a primary psychotic disorder; can you tell me whether you also have periods of clearly disorganized thinking or hallucinations/voices that occur outside of the depressive state? Also, have you had any formal assessment or treatment so far, and do you notice any social withdrawal or loss of interest/pleasure (anhedonia) since this began? REQUEST TEST: CBC_with_diff REQUEST TEST: CMP REQUEST TEST: TSH REQUEST TEST: Urine_drug_screen REQUEST TEST: B12_folate REQUEST TEST: MRI_or_CTH_brain_if_indicated_by_clinical_exam Doctor: We’ll use labs to rule out medical/substance causes, and I also want to quickly screen for depression severity and psychosis features—any chance you can rate your depression 0–10 and describe a typical day’s symptoms?

RESULTS: CBC_with_diff: NORMAL READINGS. CMP: NORMAL READINGS. TSH: NORMAL READINGS. Urine drug screen: Negative (no substances detected). B12/folate: NORMAL READINGS. MRI/CT head if indicated: Brain MRI shows no acute abnormalities. Additional clinical measurements available: - Vital signs: Temp 36.8°C (98°F), BP 115/75 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, RR 14 breaths/min. - Mental status: Withdrawn with minimal self-care; slow monotonous speech; “empty inside” mood; constricted affect; linear but impaired thought process due to auditory hallucinations; auditory hallucinations with derogatory content and feelings of worthlessness; occasionally appears to listen to someone (attention to ceiling). Cognition appears oriented; insight/judgment not fully assessed (likely impaired). No depression 0–10 rating or formal assessment/treatment details are provided in the available data.

Doctor: Thank you—at this point we have ruled out common medical/substance causes (normal CBC/CMP/TSH, negative urine drug screen, normal MRI, and no bipolar-type history). Over the next few questions, I need to distinguish whether this is major depression with psychotic features versus a primary psychotic disorder: are you able to clearly say whether the voices and paranoia only occur during the depressed periods, and do you have major loss of interest/pleasure (anhedonia) most days? Also, have you ever had any weeks-long period where the voices persisted without prominent depressed mood?

Patient: The voices and feeling worthless have mostly gone along with my persistent sadness, and I can’t really say they occur only when I’m “not” depressed. I do have trouble feeling any pleasure or interest most days, and it doesn’t seem to come and go. I haven’t had a weeks-long period where the voices continued without the depressed mood.

Doctor: Thanks—so the voices and worthlessness track closely with a persistent depressive state, with anhedonia most days, and no episodes of psychosis occurring in the absence of depression. Given this pattern and your lack of mania history or substance/medical triggers, my leading diagnosis is **major depressive disorder, severe, with psychotic features**; to confirm urgency, do you feel safe right now and are you able to stay away from any means of self-harm? Doctor: DIAGNOSIS READY: **Major Depressive Disorder, severe, with psychotic features (psychotic depression)**
